title: Independent private-pay non-medical home care agency (Chicago suburbs)
subindustry: Non-medical home care / companion & personal care
product_service: Hourly and live-in non-medical in-home care (bathing, dressing, meals, companionship, dementia supervision, respite) for seniors and disabled adults, billed hourly; IDPH-licensed Home Services Agency.
target_customer: Adult children (45-70) arranging care for aging parents; seniors with private funds or long-term-care insurance; referral sources: hospital/SNF discharge planners, senior living, elder-law attorneys, geriatric care managers.
purchase_motivation: Keeping a parent safe at home after a fall/hospitalization or dementia progression; avoiding assisted living cost; caregiver burnout.
spending_evidence: Home Instead franchisees averaged $2.61M gross sales in 2024 across 603 units, ~78k client hours each [B, WS04-S003]; Addus HomeCare (public) runs large personal-care operations with ~33% gross margin [B, WS04-S004].
representative_operators: Home Instead franchise network - 603 U.S. franchised units, avg $2.61M 2024 gross sales [B, WS04-S003]
Addus HomeCare - public, Illinois its largest personal-care market (mostly Medicaid) [B, WS04-S004]
Many independent local agencies (count MISSING)
revenue_mechanism: Hourly bill rate x client hours (minimum shift lengths, e.g., 3-4 h); live-in day rates; private pay and LTC-insurance assignment.
typical_transaction_value: ~$33 gross sales per client hour (Home Instead 2024 national average = $2.61M / 78,428 h) [B, WS04-S003]; typical client 15-40 h/week = ~$2,000-5,500/month [E].
direct_costs: Caregiver wages (IL floor $15/h [A, WS04-S025]; market rate higher, MISSING), payroll taxes, workers' comp, overtime, mileage, training, background checks.
contribution_profit_note: At ~$33/h bill and ~$21-23/h fully loaded caregiver cost, ~$10-12/h contribution before office overhead [E]; incumbent gross margin ~33% [B, WS04-S004].
working_capital_note: Caregivers paid weekly/biweekly; private-pay clients can be billed weekly in advance or card-on-file; LTC insurers reimburse in arrears (30-60 days) - finance via deposits/retainers.
sales_cycle: Days to 2 weeks for a family in crisis; referral-source development takes 6-18 months.
repeat_purchase: recurring-contract - ongoing weekly hours until client passes or moves to facility (avg duration MISSING).
acquisition_channels: Hospital/SNF discharge planner and social worker relationships
Senior living and independent living communities
Elder-law attorneys, financial planners, geriatric care managers
customer_accessibility: Families search actively in crisis, but search results are dominated by franchises and paid lead aggregators; referral relationships take persistent in-person selling.
supplier_accessibility: 'Supply' is caregivers: confirmed chronic shortage of direct care workers (labor pool cited as main HCBS constraint) [C, WS04-S009]; recruiting is the binding constraint.
competitive_intensity: extreme - dense Chicago-area market of franchises (Home Instead, Visiting Angels, Right at Home, etc.) and independents; low switching costs.
entry_strategy: Niche wedge: language/culture-specific care (e.g., Polish, Spanish, Korean, Hindi-speaking caregivers for immigrant elders), dementia specialization, or 24/7/live-in capability; faster start-of-care (same/next day) than franchises; strong caregiver pay/retention.
licenses: IDPH Home Services Agency license ($1,500/yr; provisional license, survey within 240 days) [A, WS04-S001, WS04-S027]; Health Care Worker Background Check (77 IAC 955) and dementia training code (77 IAC 973) [A, WS04-S027]; workers' comp, GL/professional liability, fidelity bond [E].
regulatory_barriers: Moderate: licensure survey, caregiver training/competency rules (hours not retrieved), wage-and-hour compliance (overtime for live-ins), Illinois paid leave rules.
operational_risks: Caregiver no-shows and turnover; client injury/abuse allegations; scheduling complexity; owner burnout from 24/7 on-call.
financial_risks: Overtime cost creep; workers' comp claims; slow LTC-insurance reimbursement; loss of a few large clients.
geographic_constraints: Local (caregiver travel radius); expansion via additional offices/territories.
founder_expertise: Home care operations, IDPH compliance, recruiting, referral-source selling, payroll/wage law.
staffing: Care coordinator/scheduler and recruiter by ~month 6; client care manager (RN not required for non-medical); 20-60 W-2 caregivers by year 2-3.
automation_potential: Scheduling optimization, recruiting outreach/screening, EVV/timekeeping, care-note summarization, billing; care itself remains human.
delegation_potential: High once a general manager/scheduler is in place; many agencies are owner-managed with GMs.
scalability: Multiple offices across suburbs; franchise data show mature units of $2-4.5M+ gross sales [B, WS04-S003].
expansion: Home nursing license (skilled add-on), Medicaid CCP contracting, care management, home modifications, adult day.
roic_note: $25-70k at risk plus founder time; year-3 operating profit of $30-180k implies roughly 50-250% on capital, but 12-18 months of losses first [E].
critical_assumptions: Independent (non-franchise) agency can reach $0.8-1.5M revenue by year 3, similar to 3-4-year franchise units [E]
Caregiver recruiting is achievable at wages that preserve 30%+ gross margin [E]
Private-pay demand holds in a recession [E]
unanswered_questions: Actual Chicago-area private-pay bill rates and caregiver wages (BLS OEWS not retrieved)
IDPH caregiver training hour requirements and manager qualifications (77 IAC 245 text unavailable)
Typical independent-agency EBITDA margins (no public data found)
failure_modes: Cannot staff accepted hours -> lost clients
Margin squeeze from wage increases not passed through

title: ADA Title II digital-accessibility compliance programs for small Illinois local governments
product_service: Fixed-price WCAG 2.1 AA programs for municipalities, townships, park/library/fire/sanitary districts: site + document inventory, automated+manual audit, CMS fixes, PDF remediation (or archive strategy), accessibility policy/statement, staff training, quarterly monitoring retainer.
target_customer: Village/city administrators, clerks, IT/communications staff and district directors at Illinois units of local government with <50,000 population (deadline Apr 26, 2028) and 50k+ (Apr 26, 2027); Illinois has 6,930 local governments incl. 3,218 special districts [A, WS15-S003].
purchase_motivation: Federal ADA Title II rule compliance dates (Apr 26, 2027 / Apr 26, 2028) [A, WS15-S001]; litigation/complaint exposure; small entities lack in-house staff.
spending_evidence: DOJ estimates the one-year delay alone saves entities ~$395M/yr annualized (~$210M/yr to small entities), implying multi-billion compliance spending nationally [A, WS15-S001]. Illinois-specific spend: MISSING.
representative_operators: Level Access, Deque, TPGi (enterprise accessibility vendors; revenue not verified) [E]
CivicPlus/Revize/Granicus (government CMS vendors bundling accessibility) [E]
AudioEye/UserWay overlay vendors (overlays widely criticized as insufficient) [E]
revenue_mechanism: One-time program fee ($3k-$25k by entity size) plus monitoring/remediation retainer ($150-$1,000/mo) [E].
typical_transaction_value: $5k-$15k initial for a small village/district; $2k-$10k/yr retainer [E]
direct_costs: Auditor/remediator labor (US or offshore), testing tools licenses, PDF remediation labor, assistive-tech manual testing time.
contribution_profit_note: ~$3k-$8k contribution per small-entity program plus ~$1.5k-$6k/yr retainer contribution [E].
working_capital_note: Local governments pay net-30 to net-60 after board approval; deposits uncommon; low inventory.
sales_cycle: 1-6 months (board/council meeting cycles; small purchases under local bid thresholds can be approved by administrators) [E]
repeat_purchase: recurring-contract: monitoring retainer; content keeps changing so remediation never ends
acquisition_channels: Direct outreach to clerks/administrators using Census/IEPA/association lists
Illinois Municipal League, IAPD (park districts), library system conferences
Partnerships with municipal website vendors and IT MSPs
Free automated scan reports as door-opener
customer_accessibility: Good: all entities and their websites are public; small entities are reachable by email/phone; procurement is often informal below bid thresholds [E].
supplier_accessibility: Confirmed: testing tools (axe, WAVE, screen readers) are freely/commercially available; remediation labor hireable [E].
competitive_intensity: moderate-high: national vendors and CMS providers target governments; overlays sold cheaply; few Illinois-focused small-entity specialists observed [E].
entry_strategy: Productized fixed-fee packages for the long tail of special districts/townships that national vendors ignore; publish Illinois deadline guidance; bundle PDF archive strategy to reduce scope; offer certification-free but documented conformance reports.
licenses: None required; standard business registration and E&O insurance advisable [E]. No professional license applies to accessibility auditing.
regulatory_barriers: Demand depends on a rule DOJ says it may substantively revise [A, WS15-S001]; SBA Advocacy recommended withdrawal for small governments [C, WS15-S002].
operational_risks: Scope creep in legacy PDFs; quality failures if over-reliant on automated scans; government website platform lock-in.
financial_risks: Demand cliff if DOJ narrows/withdraws the rule for small entities; slow municipal payments.
geographic_constraints: Remote-deliverable; Illinois focus is a sales choice, nationally applicable.
founder_expertise: WCAG 2.1/2.2 techniques, assistive-tech testing, PDF/UA remediation; CPACC/WAS credentials optional.
staffing: Founder sells + audits first; hire 1-3 remediation specialists (or offshore partner) by month 6-12.
automation_potential: AI-assisted triage of scan results, alt-text drafting, PDF tagging suggestions, report generation; manual AT testing and judgment stay human.
delegation_potential: Good with SOPs: auditing and remediation are teachable roles; sales relationships transferable.
scalability: Can expand to other states' local governments and to K-12/universities; capped by regulatory demand durability.
expansion: Document remediation production (WS15-002), vendor ACRs (WS15-003), Title III private clients, website rebuilds.
roic_note: Asset-light: <$15k at risk; ROIC potentially >300% if demand materializes [E].
critical_assumptions: Small entities will buy before the 2028 date despite possible DOJ revision
Price points of $5k-$15k are acceptable to small districts
Manual audit + remediation can be delivered at 45%+ margin
unanswered_questions: What share of Illinois small entities have already contracted for compliance?
Will DOJ's announced NPRM narrow scope (e.g., K-12, small entities)?
Typical Illinois local bid thresholds for professional services
Actual price points paid by comparable municipalities (procurement awards)
failure_modes: Race to the bottom with overlays/cheap scans
Long municipal sales cycles drain founder time
